findings.path: scripts/finalizer-e2e.sh — shell wait-for-device without explicit timeout (non-blocking observation)
findings.problem: After 'adb kill-server' + 'adb start-server', the shell script calls 'adb wait-for-device' without an explicit timeout (the JS adbReconnect() bounds it at 30s). If the emulator failed to re-register with the new server, this could block until the runner kills the step. This matches the pristine pattern (the previous 'adb reconnect' path also used an unbounded wait-for-device), and emulator re-registration with a restarted adb server is standard, reliable behavior (the server scans the emulator console/adb ports on localhost), so the risk is theoretical; a failed restart is otherwise handled gracefully (getprop checks print 'unknown', install fails with diagnostics rather than hanging).
findings.evidence: scripts/finalizer-e2e.sh lines 68-77 and 130-137: 'adb kill-server 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 3; adb start-server 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 2; adb wait-for-device 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 1'. Pristine finalizer-e2e.sh used the same unbounded wait-for-device after 'adb reconnect'. JS adbReconnect() bounds wait-for-device at 30s.
